case.title: The diagnosis the patient brought with him — two days of black stool, a normal first hemoglobin, and a bleeding duodenal ulcer behind the word 'gastritis'
case.synthetic_note: SYNTHETIC CASE. The patient is an authored fiction built for teaching; no real patient data exists in this module. His words are authored to carry the case's anchoring event: the benign diagnosis he supplies about himself. The endoscopy is an authored encounter; the imaging link is a localisation to a real segmentation of a different person, and says so. The physiology link prices mechanism, not this patient, and its gaps are part of the case.
case.presentation: A 71-year-old retired joiner comes to the emergency department because his stool has been black and tarry for two days and he feels light-headed when he stands. He is not distressed, and he explains himself before anyone examines him: 'It's my gastritis again. It flares up every winter, burns for a few days, and settles with the pink medicine and plain food. Two winters ago they wanted to keep me in and do tests, and it was nothing.' He has had two similar episodes in past winters — black stool and epigastric burning — both self-treated, neither investigated; the word 'gastritis' is his own, and no clinician has ever looked inside him. He takes ibuprofen 400 mg most days for knee osteoarthritis, bought over the counter, for about four years, without gastroprotection; no aspirin, anticoagulant or antiplatelet agent. He drinks about two units of alcohol a week. He has not vomited blood, has not fainted, has lost no weight and eats normally between episodes.

history: Two prior episodes of black stool with epigastric burning in past winters, self-treated, never investigated; the diagnosis 'gastritis' is his own and has never been scoped or otherwise tested (case data).
Ibuprofen 400 mg on most days for about four years for knee osteoarthritis, self-medicated, no gastroprotection; no aspirin, anticoagulant or antiplatelet agent (case data).
Alcohol about two units a week; no liver disease, no cardiac failure, weight stable (case data).

presentation_stages.title: Arrival: his history, the examination, and the finger
presentation_stages.narrative: Emergency department, triage and first assessment. He gives his history - and his diagnosis - himself; the examination and the rectal examination are done; the arrival vitals are taken. The learner must commit a stage-1 board on this evidence alone, with the Glasgow-Blatchford block partially computable (the blood items unmeasured).

presentation_stages.title: First bloods and the standing test: the score completes
presentation_stages.narrative: Emergency department, monitored cubicle. The admission bloods and the orthostatic vitals land: the score completes at 6, the urea ratio prices the source, and the first hemoglobin - normal - does its quiet work on the board. The disposition argument happens here.

presentation_stages.title: Deterioration and the endoscopy: the vessel in the ulcer
presentation_stages.narrative: The six-hour reassessment witnesses fresh hematemesis; the repeat count lands at 7.6; the endoscopy, expedited, finds and treats the lesion and surveys the rest. The anchor is ruled out by arithmetic in this stage and retired by anatomy in the same hour.

presentation_stages.title: After hemostasis: what is treated, what is stopped, what is watched
presentation_stages.narrative: Monitored ward bed, 24 hours on: no rebleed, the count stable untransfused, the urease test positive. The final board, the commitment, and the two conversations - the drug, and the diagnosis he brought with him.

hypotheses.label: Bleeding duodenal ulcer

prior.note: VERIFY-FLAGGED PLACEHOLDER, not a measurement: no consulted source gives base rates for this staged presentation in a defined population, so the split is an authoring choice for the exercise, flagged as such wherever it appears. The ulcer carries the largest placeholder share: NSAID exposure, epigastric pain and melena are the classic peptic picture, and peptic ulcer is the commonest upper-GI bleeding source in the consulted guideline populations (C66, C70) - the figure itself is a flag.

hypotheses.mondo_note: Verified against EBI OLS at Milestone 61: MONDO:0005412 'duodenal ulcer' - 'An ulcer in the duodenal wall'. Its parent class, peptic ulcer disease (MONDO:0004247), was verified at Milestone 20. The endoscopy localises the lesion to the duodenal bulb.
hypotheses.criterion: Endoscopic confirmation of the lesion, with its stigmata priced by the Forrest block and the admission severity by the Glasgow-Blatchford block (both declared in this case); no score diagnoses the lesion - the endoscope does.

hypotheses.label: Gastritis / erosive mucosal bleeding - MINOR AND SELF-LIMITED, settling without intervention (the patient's own diagnosis, in his own terms)

prior.note: VERIFY-FLAGGED PLACEHOLDER, not a measurement: no consulted source gives base rates for this staged presentation in a defined population, so the split is an authoring choice for the exercise, flagged as such wherever it appears. The anchor hypothesis is defined by the claim the patient actually makes - a minor mucosal bleed that settles on its own - because that claim, not the bare word gastritis, is what the learner is invited to adopt. Erosive disease is a real and common bleeding source (C66, C70); the placeholder prices the word, the findings price the claim.

hypotheses.mondo_note: Verified against EBI OLS at Milestone 61: MONDO:0004966 'gastritis' - 'An inflammatory process affecting the gastric mucosa'. The hypothesis's severity claim is the patient's, recorded in its label; the Mondo class names the inflammation, not the claim.
hypotheses.criterion: As stated, the hypothesis is a severity claim, and it is priced as one: the Rational Clinical Examination's likelihood ratios for SEVERE upper-GI bleeding (C64) are entered against it in reciprocal form, and the Glasgow-Blatchford block prices the same claim independently. Endoscopy retires it anatomically: the stomach is normal.

hypotheses.label: Bleeding oesophageal varices

prior.note: VERIFY-FLAGGED PLACEHOLDER, not a measurement: no consulted source gives base rates for this staged presentation in a defined population, so the split is an authoring choice for the exercise, flagged as such wherever it appears. A dangerous source that must stay on the board at presentation; no sourced prevalence for this presentation was consulted.

hypotheses.mondo_note: Verified against EBI OLS at Milestone 61: MONDO:0001221 'esophageal varices' - dilated submucosal veins in the lower oesophagus, usually from portal hypertension. No liver disease is in this history (f.hepatic-disease, absent), and the endoscopy survey finds no varices.
hypotheses.criterion: Varices bleed from portal hypertension; with no hepatic-disease history and a normal oesophagus at endoscopy the hypothesis is retired by inspection, not by a ratio.

hypotheses.label: Mallory-Weiss tear

prior.note: VERIFY-FLAGGED PLACEHOLDER, not a measurement: no consulted source gives base rates for this staged presentation in a defined population, so the split is an authoring choice for the exercise, flagged as such wherever it appears. A standard member of the upper-GI bleeding differential; no sourced prevalence for this presentation was consulted.

hypotheses.mondo_note: Verified against EBI OLS at Milestone 61: MONDO:0043247 'Mallory-Weiss syndrome' - a mucosal laceration at the gastro-oesophageal junction, usually after forceful retching. His vomiting begins two days AFTER the melena (f.hematemesis, stage 3), the wrong order for the mechanism, and the junction is normal at endoscopy.
hypotheses.criterion: The tear follows forceful retching; here the bleeding precedes any vomiting by two days, and the gastro-oesophageal junction is inspected and normal.

hypotheses.label: Bleeding gastric malignancy

prior.note: VERIFY-FLAGGED PLACEHOLDER, not a measurement: no consulted source gives base rates for this staged presentation in a defined population, so the split is an authoring choice for the exercise, flagged as such wherever it appears. Kept on the board in a 71-year-old with upper-GI bleeding until the stomach is inspected; no sourced prevalence for this presentation was consulted.

hypotheses.mondo_note: Verified against EBI OLS at Milestone 61: MONDO:0001056 'gastric cancer'. No weight loss or appetite change is in the history (f.weight-loss, absent), and the stomach is normal at endoscopy.
hypotheses.criterion: Retired by direct inspection of a normal stomach, and unsupported before it: no systemic features are present.

hypotheses.label: A lower gastrointestinal source (the melena is not from above the ligament of Treitz)

prior.note: VERIFY-FLAGGED PLACEHOLDER, not a measurement: no consulted source gives base rates for this staged presentation in a defined population, so the split is an authoring choice for the exercise, flagged as such wherever it appears. The live alternative at arrival: melena usually means an upper source, but 'usually' is a claim the examination and the urea ratio price in this case (C64).

hypotheses.mondo_note: REFUSAL RECORDED at Milestone 61: two EBI OLS searches ('lower gastrointestinal hemorrhage'; 'diverticular disease') returned no Mondo class. The hypothesis names a bleeding-source LOCATION, not one disease; its likeliest single lesion, colonic diverticulosis, carries a phenotype term (HP:0002253) but no Mondo class verified in this pass, and coding the hypothesis to diverticulitis - an inflammation he does not have - would be inventing an ontology. The class is left null with this refusal on the record.
hypotheses.criterion: Priced by the two consulted ratios that speak to source location (C64): melenic stool on EXAMINATION (LR 25 for an upper source) and a urea:creatinine ratio above 30 (summary LR 7.5), each entered here in the machinery's reciprocal direction.

findings.text: 71 years old (case data). Age prices nothing on this board directly; it prices the transfusion conversation (C65's trial population), the stakes of the malignancy hypothesis, and the physiology link's stated gap - the engine's subject is a standard adult, not a 71-year-old.

The patient supplies his own diagnosis, confidently and from experience, in the first minute: 'It's my gastritis again. It flares up every winter, burns for a few days, and settles with the pink medicine and plain food. Two winters ago they wanted to keep me in and do tests, and it was nothing.' The label is his own coinage, carried for years; no clinician has scoped him and no record supports it (case data - the encounter itself is the source for what he says). This finding is the case's anchoring event: a diagnosis installed by the historian, at presentation, before any evidence is in.

Two prior episodes in past winters - black stool and epigastric burning - self-treated with antacids and plain food, both settling over days, NEITHER investigated (case data). The detail that makes his frame feel proven is the detail that should break it: the prior episodes were never tested, so their settling proves only that he survived them; a duodenal ulcer bleeds, stops, and bleeds again, and an unscoped 'gastritis' and an unscoped ulcer are the same story told twice.

Black, tarry stools for two days, by his report (case data). The Rational Clinical Examination prices patient-REPORTED melena at LR range 5.1-5.9 for an upper-GI source (C64); this case registers NO ratio for the report, because the examination finding below supersedes it in the same source and the machinery prices each stage's evidence once - the report is carried here as history, the finger prices it.

Digital rectal examination: black, tarry, sticky stool, frankly melenic, no fresh blood (case data). Srygley 2012 prices melenic stool ON EXAMINATION at LR 25 (95% CI 4-174) for an upper-GI over a lower-GI source (C64); the ratio is registered against the lower-source hypothesis in the reciprocal direction.

lr.note: LR- 0.04 against the lower-source hypothesis, computed as the reciprocal of the consulted LR 25 for melenic stool on examination as an upper- over lower-GI source sign (C64). Derivation in cases/parameters.json.

findings.text: Epigastric burning pain, longstanding, unchanged in character this episode, eased by antacids (case data). It is the symptom his frame is built on, and it fits the truth at least as well - peptic pain and 'gastritis' pain are the same sensation with different lesions behind them. No consulted source quantifies it for this differential, so it carries no ratio; it discriminates nothing, and the case says so rather than letting it quietly support whichever hypothesis the reader already holds.

Ibuprofen 400 mg on most days for about four years, self-medicated for knee osteoarthritis, no gastroprotection; no aspirin, anticoagulant or antiplatelet agent (case data). The exposure is the case's mechanism: NSAIDs cause and re-open peptic ulcers, and the consulted ulcer guideline is explicit that in ulcer bleeding the NSAID is stopped (C69). It carries no likelihood ratio - no consulted source quantifies NSAID history for this differential - and it does its work in management, where it is decisive.

Resting pulse 102/min at arrival, against a systolic pressure of 124 (meas.pulse-arrival; case data). Srygley 2012 prices tachycardia at LR 4.9 (95% CI 3.2-7.6) for SEVERE over non-severe upper-GI bleeding (C64). The anchor hypothesis is defined by its severity claim - minor, self-limited, no intervention - so the severity ratio is registered against it in reciprocal form: a heart rate his frame calls insignificant is, in the consulted evidence, a marker of the bleeding his frame says he does not have.

lr.note: LR- 0.2041 against the anchor hypothesis, computed as the reciprocal of the consulted LR 4.9 for tachycardia as a marker of severe over non-severe upper gastrointestinal bleeding (C64): the anchor hypothesis is defined by its severity claim, so the severity ratio prices that claim. Derivation in cases/parameters.json.

findings.text: Light-headed on standing since yesterday; no fall, no injury (case data). Presyncopal, not vertiginous: the candidate phenotype term for lightheadedness (HP:0002321) resolves in the ontology to vertigo, a spinning sensation he does not describe, and was NOT used (C11 addendum, Milestone 61). The symptom is carried by the orthostatic measurements at stage 2 and by the syncope absence below.

No loss of consciousness at any point (case data). Recorded as an explicit absence, not an omission: syncope is a scored item in the Glasgow-Blatchford block (C63), and the block's arithmetic needs the absence on the record, worth 0 of its 2 points.

No vomiting of blood or coffee-ground material before arrival (case data). The absence matters twice: it is why Mallory-Weiss starts cold (no antecedent retching), and it is the baseline against which the stage-3 hematemesis is an in-hospital event - the event the consulted guideline names as a reason to expedite endoscopy (C66).

No liver disease: no jaundice, no ascites, no encephalopathy, alcohol about two units a week (case data). A scored Glasgow-Blatchford item (C63; absent, 0 of 2 points) and the varices hypothesis's missing premise, both at once.
No cardiac failure: no orthopnoea, no oedema, no known diagnosis (case data). A scored Glasgow-Blatchford item (C63; absent, 0 of 2 points).

Weight stable, appetite normal, no night sweats (case data). The malignancy hypothesis's expected systemic company is not there; unquantified by any consulted source, so it carries no ratio - the endoscopy retires that hypothesis, not this absence.

Urea:creatinine ratio 33 (BUN 33 mg/dL over creatinine 1.0 mg/dL), above the ratio of 30 the Rational Clinical Examination prices at summary LR 7.5 (95% CI 2.8-12.0) for an upper-GI over a lower-GI source (C64); registered against the lower-source hypothesis in reciprocal form. The mechanism is the case in miniature: blood in the upper gut is digested to urea, and a falling circulating volume concentrates it further - the blood he calls gastritis is written in his chemistry.

lr.note: LR- 0.1333 against the lower-source hypothesis, computed as the reciprocal of the consulted summary LR 7.5 for a blood urea nitrogen:creatinine ratio above 30 as an upper- over lower-GI source sign (C64). Derivation in cases/parameters.json.

findings.text: The first hemoglobin is 13.9 g/dL - inside the consulted male range (C67) - and it is the most dangerous number in the case, because it invites the reader to close it. It excludes nothing. Whole blood is lost at its own concentration: at the moment bleeding stops, the hemoglobin of what remains is the hemoglobin of what was lost, and the count falls only as transcapillary refill and administered crystalloid dilute the remainder - the physiology engine's course arm computes exactly this lag (hematocrit 0.432 one minute after the loss ends, 0.399 at sixty minutes on 408 mL of refill; physiology_link). The consulted examination review prices only the far tail of the fall (hemoglobin below 8, C64); a preserved first count carries NO likelihood ratio, by design, and the case states the mechanism instead of inventing a reassurance value.

Orthostatic vitals: supine 124/76, pulse 102; after one minute standing, 104/68, pulse 126 - a systolic fall of 20 mmHg with a pulse rise of 24 (meas.sbp-standing, meas.pulse-standing; case data). A volume-depleted circulation announcing itself on the maneuver his frame never performs. No likelihood ratio is registered: the consulted review does not price orthostatic change for this question (C64), and the case carries the finding as examination evidence and as a Glasgow-Blatchford-adjacent warning, not as a number it cannot source.

About six hours after arrival, on the ward round that the admission bought, he vomits twice: coffee-ground material, then fresh red blood (case data). The bleed declares itself in the open. No likelihood ratio is registered - the consulted review prices blood in a nasogastric aspirate (LR 9.6, C64), a test this encounter never performs, and witnessed hematemesis is not a sensitivity/specificity pair in any consulted source; it does its work through the guideline instead, as an in-hospital bloody emesis that expedites the endoscopy (C66).

The repeat hemoglobin is 7.6 g/dL - below 8. Srygley 2012 prices hemoglobin below 8 g/dL at LR range 4.5-6.2 for severe over non-severe upper-GI bleeding (C64); the case registers the CONSERVATIVE end of the range (4.5) against the anchor hypothesis in reciprocal form, by the register's stated convention (C52, Milestone 54). Six grams of hemoglobin separate this count from the first; the fall is the refill-and-dilution lag of stage 2 arriving on paper, plus the ongoing loss the hematemesis witnessed.

lr.note: LR- 0.2222 against the anchor hypothesis, computed as the reciprocal of the conservative end (4.5) of the consulted LR range 4.5-6.2 for hemoglobin below 8 g/dL as a marker of severe over non-severe bleeding (C64); conservative-end registration per the register's stated convention (C52). Derivation in cases/parameters.json.

findings.text: Pale, with cool hands (case data). Carried as examination texture for the deterioration; no ratio is registered for it.

One litre of balanced crystalloid is given intravenously across the interval, resuscitation before endoscopy as the consulted guideline directs (C66). Recorded because it is part of the arithmetic of the falling hemoglobin: some of the fall between 13.9 and 7.6 is dilution by this litre and by the refill the engine prices - and the rest is ongoing loss, which the hematemesis witnessed. The case does not decompose the fall further; the bedside cannot, and it says so.

Upper endoscopy: an 18 mm ulcer on the posterior wall of the duodenal bulb; the remaining duodenum is normal (case data - the authored encounter). This is the ground truth, seen, not inferred: the lesion his four years of ibuprofen made and his two winters of 'gastritis' described.

In the ulcer base, a non-bleeding visible vessel - a Forrest IIa stigma (case data). The consulted guideline recommends endoscopic hemostasis for a visible vessel (C66); it is a Forrest-block input, declared as its own finding so the classification's arithmetic is auditable.

No active spurting or oozing at inspection (case data). A Forrest-block input, recorded as an explicit absence: the vessel is visible but not bleeding at the moment of the examination - which is what makes the class IIa and not I.
No adherent clot in the ulcer base (case data). A Forrest-block input, recorded as an explicit absence.
No flat pigmented spot (case data). A Forrest-block input, recorded as an explicit absence.
The ulcer base is not clean - it carries the vessel (case data). A Forrest-block input, recorded as an explicit absence so the classification cannot be satisfied by a default.

Combination endoscopic therapy: dilute epinephrine injected around the vessel and two through-the-scope clips placed across it; hemostasis achieved, no rebleeding during the examination (case data). The pattern is the consulted guideline's: epinephrine is never the sole modality for high-risk stigmata - a mechanical or thermal second modality does the durable work (C66), and the second consulted guideline concurs (C70).

The survey is otherwise normal: oesophagus without varices or tear; stomach without erosions, ulcer or mass (case data). This single negative retires three hypotheses anatomically - the anchor (no gastritis, no erosions, anywhere), the varices, the malignancy - and it carries no likelihood ratio: direct inspection is not a sensitivity/specificity pair in any consulted source, and the case states that rather than pricing the look.

Rapid urease test on an antral biopsy: positive - Helicobacter pylori present (case data). The second half of the ulcer's etiology, beside the NSAID. The consulted ulcer guideline's management is explicit: a patient whose bleeding ulcer is H. pylori-associated receives eradication therapy, and eradication is documented (C69).

No further melena or hematemesis in the 24 hours after hemostasis; the post-endoscopy hemoglobin is 7.7 g/dL, unchanged in substance from the nadir (case data). The bleeding has stopped; what remains is the watching, the acid suppression, and the two causes to remove.

labs.interpretation: Inside the consulted male range (C67) - the preserved, lagging first count. See f.hemoglobin-preserved for why this number excludes nothing.
Above the consulted range (C47). Four points in the Glasgow-Blatchford block (band 28-70, C63), and the numerator of the ratio finding.
Inside the consulted male range (C68): the kidneys are not the story - which is what makes the urea elevation a blood-and-volume signal rather than a renal one. The denominator of the ratio finding.
Below 8: the finding f.hemoglobin-below-8, and the case's transfusion question - answered against the restrictive threshold at management.

Still rising with ongoing bleeding and digestion of blood. Recorded as course data; the Blatchford block prices ADMISSION values only and does not re-open for it - the score's validated use is the admission, and the case keeps that discipline rather than re-pricing a deterioration the Forrest block and the board already carry.
Stable at the nadir's level with no transfusion given - the empirical answer to the transfusion question, recorded after the disposition it supports.

measurements.name: Pulse at arrival (resting)
measurements.interpretation: The tachycardia finding (f.tachycardia) and a Glasgow-Blatchford item (pulse 100 or more, 1 point, C63).

measurements.name: Systolic BP at arrival
measurements.interpretation: A Glasgow-Blatchford item (110 or more, 0 points, C63) and the supine baseline of the orthostatic pair.

measurements.name: Diastolic BP after 1 minute standing
measurements.interpretation: Standing pulse pressure 36 mmHg - narrowing as the volume falls (case data).

measurements.name: Pulse 24 h after hemostasis
measurements.interpretation: Settling with the bleeding stopped (case data).

available_tests.name: Admission bloods (hemoglobin, urea, creatinine)
available_tests.note: The bloods that complete the Glasgow-Blatchford block and price the source. Resource figures are verify-flagged placeholders by the house rule.

available_tests.name: Orthostatic vital signs
available_tests.note: Supine and one-minute standing pressures and pulses. Costs a nurse, a cuff and sixty seconds; the anchor never orders it because the anchor has already decided there is nothing to find.

available_tests.name: Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy
available_tests.note: The diagnostic and therapeutic act of the case: finds the lesion, classifies its stigmata (Forrest), and treats the vessel in the same session. Performed early (within 24 hours of admission, C66) and expedited by the in-hospital hematemesis. Resource figures are verify-flagged placeholders by the house rule.

available_tests.name: Serial hemoglobin (repeat count at reassessment)
available_tests.note: The repeat count that catches the lag arriving: the first hemoglobin's reassurance has an expiry time, and this test is how the case enforces it. Resource figures are verify-flagged placeholders by the house rule.

available_tests.name: Interval reassessment (ward review at six hours)
available_tests.note: The scheduled re-examination of an admitted bleeder: witnesses the hematemesis, the pallor, the stage-3 pressures, and gives the resuscitation litre. It is the admission - the refusal of the patient's discharge plan - that puts a clinician in the room when the bleed declares.

available_tests.name: Post-endoscopy review (24-hour count, biopsy urease, course)
available_tests.note: The morning-after bundle: the stable count, the H. pylori result that completes the etiology, and the no-rebleed course the disposition is built on. Resource figures are verify-flagged placeholders by the house rule.

criteria_blocks.label: Glasgow-Blatchford score
criteria_blocks.system: Blatchford 2000 (C63): the admission score for upper-GI bleeding, built from the ADMISSION bloods and vitals and the presentation features - and in this case it prices exactly those: every item below references an arrival vital, a first blood, or a presentation finding, and no later value ever re-enters it. The score's validated question is who needs an intervention, not what the lesion is. A partial total, while any item is unmeasured, is a floor and not a reading - the case's stage-1 board shows it that way on purpose, because a partially-computed 2 is how the anchor would quote it.

items.label: Blood urea nitrogen (Blatchford's bands, mg/dL)
items.text: His admission BUN is 33 mg/dL: 4 points (C63).

items.label: Hemoglobin - men's bands
items.text: His ADMISSION hemoglobin is 13.9 g/dL: 0 points (C63). The stage-3 count of 7.6 does not re-enter this item - the score prices the admission, and the discipline is the point: the instrument that was reassuring about his blood count was built to be read once, at the door, alongside the items that were not reassuring.

items.label: Presentation with syncope
items.text: Absent - he has not fainted: 0 of 2 points (C63).

bands.label: very low risk
bands.text: GBS 0-1: the consulted guideline's threshold for considering outpatient management with outpatient endoscopy (C66). Nothing in this case's course comes near it once the bloods land - and the stage-1 PARTIAL total of 2 already excludes it.

bands.status: below the high-risk band on the assessed items
bands.label: below Blatchford's high-risk band, on the assessed items
bands.text: While any item is unmeasured this total is a floor, not a reading: the two items unmeasured at stage 1 carry up to 12 of the scale's 23 points between them. Read with the partial flag, or not read at all.

bands.status: high risk of needing intervention (GBS 6 or more)
bands.label: high risk of needing intervention
bands.text: GBS 6 or more: in Blatchford's validation group, scores of 6 or more were associated with a greater than 50 percent risk of needing an intervention - transfusion, endoscopic therapy or surgery - or of dying (C63). His completed score is 6: admission and hospital-based management, whatever his own diagnosis says.

criteria_blocks.label: Forrest classification of the ulcer's stigmata
criteria_blocks.system: The Forrest classification, as the consulted ESGE guideline operationalises it (C66): stigmata are priced by what they predict and therefore by what they demand - active bleeding (I) and a non-bleeding visible vessel (IIa) are high-risk and receive endoscopic hemostasis; an adherent clot (IIb) is considered for therapy; a flat spot (IIc) and a clean base (III) receive none. The classification is Forrest's (1974), cited here through the guideline that prices its consequence, not through the original paper, which was not consulted. Inputs are the endoscopy findings only, each recorded present or absent as its own finding so no class is reached by default.
criteria_blocks.pending_label: not yet classifiable - endoscopy has not been performed

result.label: active bleeding - high-risk stigmata: combination endoscopic hemostasis (epinephrine plus a second modality) (C66)
non-bleeding visible vessel - high-risk stigmata: endoscopic hemostasis (thermal, mechanical or sclerosant, alone or combined with epinephrine) (C66)
adherent clot - endoscopic therapy may be considered (C66)
flat pigmented spot - low-risk stigmata: no endoscopic hemostasis
clean base - low-risk stigmata: no endoscopic hemostasis

adjudication.diagnosis_label: Bleeding duodenal ulcer (18 mm, posterior wall of the duodenal bulb) with a non-bleeding visible vessel - Forrest IIa - in a long-term NSAID user with H. pylori; the 'gastritis' was never scoped, and the lesion behind it bled for two days behind a normal first hemoglobin

glasgow_blatchford.reading: GBS 6 - Blatchford's band in which more than half the validation group needed an intervention or died (C63); the score completed at stage 2 on admission values and never re-priced.
glasgow_blatchford.composition: BUN 33 (4) + pulse 102 (1) + melena (1); hemoglobin 13.9 (0), SBP 124 (0), syncope/hepatic/cardiac all absent (0). The reassuring item is the one the mechanism explains away - see f.hemoglobin-preserved.

forrest.reading: Non-bleeding visible vessel: high-risk stigmata, endoscopic hemostasis indicated and performed (C66).

transfusion.reading: No transfusion: the nadir stays above the restrictive threshold of the consulted trial (transfuse below 7 g/dL, target 7-9; C65), concordant with both consulted guidelines' restrictive stance (C66, C70). The trial's exclusions - massive exsanguinating bleeding, acute coronary syndrome - do not apply to him. The 24-hour count (7.7, untransfused) is recorded as the outcome of that decision.

criteria_comparison.board_final_leader: hyp.duodenal-ulcer at 0.5376 on the workbench board - the board is carried by the two priced directions (source location; severity against the anchor) and the endoscopy then settles what boards cannot: the lesion, seen.
criteria_comparison.anchor_retired_by: Anatomy: the endoscopy survey finds a normal stomach - the anchor hypothesis's organ is inspected and empty - after the arithmetic had already ruled it out at stage 3 (0.0186) on the severity ratios.
criteria_comparison.note: No score in this case diagnoses anything: the Blatchford block prices the admission, the Forrest block prices the stigma, the board prices the differential. The diagnosis is the endoscopist's sentence, and the case keeps the three instruments separate on purpose.

excluded.basis: Ruled out arithmetically at stage 3 (0.0186) by the severity ratios (C64), then retired anatomically: the stomach at endoscopy shows no gastritis and no erosions - the frame's organ is empty. As a bare word it names a real disease; as the patient used it - minor, self-limited, settle at home - it is the case's refuted claim.
Ruled out at stage 1 (0.0071) by the examination melena (LR 25, C64) and driven further down at stage 2 by the urea:creatinine ratio (summary LR 7.5, C64).
No hepatic disease in the history and a normal oesophagus at endoscopy.
The mechanism's order is reversed - bleeding precedes vomiting by two days - and the gastro-oesophageal junction is normal at endoscopy.
No systemic features, and a normal stomach at endoscopy.

adjudication.note: Ground truth is the endoscopy: an 18 mm posterior duodenal-bulb ulcer with a visible vessel, treated to hemostasis, in a man whose own diagnosis had explained the same symptoms away for years. The adjudication's discipline is the case's: the scores price severity and stigmata, the board prices the differential, and neither is allowed to impersonate the diagnosis.

ground_truth.diagnosis: Bleeding duodenal ulcer (18 mm, posterior wall of the duodenal bulb), Forrest IIa visible vessel, combination endoscopic hemostasis; NSAID-associated and H. pylori-positive; Glasgow-Blatchford 6 on admission values; nadir hemoglobin 7.6 g/dL, untransfused under the restrictive threshold; the patient's 'gastritis' - never investigated in two prior episodes - was the ulcer's bleeding all along.
ground_truth.engine_state: The physiology baseline link is the pinned resting run (hash 0x6369b10e9a71c872, identical to cases 1-8). The hemorrhage arms are this case's working links. The 750 mL arm's post window (pulse 102.1, MAP defended at 68.9 while stroke volume falls to 33.9 mL and pulse pressure narrows to 23.2 mmHg) prices the compensation PATTERN the arrival vitals show. The course arm prices the LAG the first hemoglobin must be read against: its hematocrit is 0.432 one minute after the 1,500 mL loss ends - essentially the pre-bleed value, because whole blood leaves at its own concentration - and 0.399 at sixty minutes, after 408.0 mL of transcapillary refill has diluted what remains. His 13.9 is that physics, at his tempo. The gaps are part of the truth and are stated in physiology_link: the engine bleeds in seconds where he bled over two days; its subject is a standard adult, not 71; it has no gut lumen, no ulcer, no endoscopy - and no urea state, so the BUN this case prices is authored data the engine cannot check.

hpo_absent.label: Syncope
hpo_absent.note: Asserted as an explicit ABSENCE (verified against EBI OLS at Milestone 61): he is light-headed but has never lost consciousness - the distinction is a scored Glasgow-Blatchford item (C63) and the reason the lightheadedness is carried by the orthostatic term instead.

ground_truth.mondo_note: Verified against EBI OLS at Milestone 61 (C10 addendum): 'An ulcer in the duodenal wall'. No separate bleeding-ulcer class is asserted: hemorrhage is this case's presentation, not a distinct ontology term, and the parent class (peptic ulcer disease, MONDO:0004247) was verified at Milestone 20.

physiology_link.baseline_command: cd physiology && cargo run --release -- run resting
physiology_link.hemorrhage_command: cd physiology && cargo run --release -- run hemorrhage
physiology_link.hemorrhage_scenario: CaseKind::Hemorrhage750: 750 mL of external loss over 60 s from the engaged resting state. The recorded outputs are the run's own post window - the window the physiology gates price (the post-window pulse of 102.1/min sits inside the ATLS Class II band recorded in physiology/parameters.json). The arm prices the compensation PATTERN: mean pressure defended (72.9 to 68.9 mmHg) while stroke volume more than halves and the pulse pressure narrows - rate doing the work volume no longer can. That is the shape of his arrival vitals (124/76, pulse 102, and a pulse pressure that narrows to 36 on standing): the numerical nearness of the arm's post pulse (102.1) to his (102) is a coincidence of bands, NOT an identity, and the case does not claim it as one.
physiology_link.course_command: cd physiology && cargo run --release -- run course
physiology_link.course_scenario: The untreated course arm (a 1,500 mL loss run over 60 minutes, Milestones 24-26): the hematocrit one minute after the loss is 0.432 - still effectively the pre-bleed value, because whole blood is lost at its own concentration - and 0.399 at sixty minutes, after a measured 408.04 mL of net transcapillary refill has diluted the remainder. This arm is the case's central mechanism: it is why a man two days into a significant bleed can present with a hemoglobin inside the normal range, and why the case forbids the first count from closing anything.
physiology_link.gap_statement: The link is mechanistic, and its limits are stated, not smoothed. TEMPO: the engine's losses run over 60 seconds and 60 minutes; his ran over about two days of ooze - the compensation pattern and the hematocrit lag transfer, the magnitudes do not, and no engine number is presented as his volume lost. SUBJECT: the engine's circulation is a standard adult's; he is 71, and reflex ageing is not modelled. ANATOMY: the engine has no gastrointestinal tract, no ulcer, no vessel and no endoscope - nothing in it can confirm or deny the lesion. CHEMISTRY: urea is not an engine state (Milestone 30: glucose and urea are carried as the constant term of plasma osmolality), so the BUN course this case prices through Blatchford and the ratio finding is authored clinical data the engine cannot check. FLUIDS: the crystalloid litre is an encounter event recorded in the findings; the course arm's crystalloid variant exists in the engine but is not linked here, because the case's claim needs only the untreated lag.
physiology_link.verification: The checker re-runs the hemorrhage arm at every validation (it completes in under a second) and compares the trace hash and every recorded post-window output. The course arm's hematocrit marks are pinned by identity with the Milestone 26 dossier's printed course table (0.432 at +1 min, 0.399 at +60 min) and its trace hash with the Milestone 30 dossier; the course command takes about a minute, so the workbench pins it by those identities rather than re-running it, and the net-refill figure (408.04 mL) is the value the run printed when measured at Milestone 61, recorded in that dossier.

The link localises the ORGAN the endoscopy found the ulcer in - it does not show the ulcer, and the honesty block says why it cannot.

label.name: duodenum
label.mapping_note: TotalSegmentator label 'duodenum', crosswalk index 10, mapped to Body Model record canal.duodenum (data/digestive/digestive-inventory.json). The ulcer sits in the duodenal bulb - the first part of this organ; the segmentation carries the organ whole and does not subdivide it.

ulcer_label_absence.statement: The 104-label TotalSegmentator set holds organ labels only: no ulcer, erosion or stigmata label exists in it, and none was invented for this case. A duodenal ulcer is a mucosal lesion found by looking at the mucosa - endoscopically - not a structure a CT segmentation carries; this case's diagnostic act is the endoscopy, and the imaging link's only claim is anatomical.

imaging_link.honesty_block: Three individuals, never conflated (the standing honesty discipline of this module): the Body Model record is a canonical anatomical description; the imaging subject s0778 is a real scanned 57-year-old man whose CT this is not the CT of; the case patient is an authored 71-year-old. The duodenum label statistics describe the imaging subject's organ. The atlas mesh is a fourth individual again and no co-registration with any of them is claimed. The series is watermarked synthetic teaching data, and its label set holds no ulcer - the endoscopy is an authored encounter, and the case says so wherever the link is used.

management.disposition: ADMIT to a monitored bed - the disposition the completed Glasgow-Blatchford score (6, C63) and the orthostatic drop jointly demand, and the refusal of the patient's own plan. High-dose intravenous proton-pump inhibition after hemostasis: 80 mg bolus then 8 mg/h for 72 hours (C66), concordant with the second consulted guideline (C70), then oral PPI. Endoscopy performed early - within 24 hours of admission (C66) - and expedited when the in-hospital hematemesis met the guideline's very-early criteria (C66). Observation through the 72-hour high-dose window on a monitored bed, with serial hemoglobins; discharge when the count is stable, the stool is clearing, and the safety-netting below is understood.
management.endoscopic_therapy: Combination therapy at the index endoscopy: epinephrine injection plus two through-the-scope clips across the visible vessel, hemostasis achieved (f.endoscopy-hemostasis). Epinephrine alone is explicitly not the consulted standard for high-risk stigmata (C66, C70).
management.transfusion_decision: NO transfusion. Nadir 7.6 g/dL against the restrictive threshold of the consulted trial - transfuse below 7 g/dL, target 7-9 (C65) - with both consulted guidelines restrictive in concord (C66: target 7-9 g/dL; C70: threshold 7 g/dL). The trial's exclusions (massive exsanguinating bleeding, acute coronary syndrome) do not apply. The untransfused 24-hour count of 7.7 is the recorded outcome; the decision is revisited instantly by any rebleed, symptom or further fall.
management.nsaid: Ibuprofen STOPPED, permanently, and recorded as such in his notes and to his GP: the consulted ulcer guideline is explicit that NSAIDs are stopped in ulcer bleeding, and if one ever had to be resumed it would be a low-dose COX-2-selective agent with a PPI (C69). His knee is managed otherwise (topical agents, physiotherapy, paracetamol within dose) - the analgesia plan is part of the discharge, not an afterthought, because an unmanaged knee is how he would quietly restart the drug.
management.h_pylori: Eradication therapy for the positive urease test, with eradication DOCUMENTED after the acute phase (C69): a bleeding ulcer associated with H. pylori is treated for the infection, and once eradication is documented, maintenance antisecretory therapy is generally not needed unless NSAIDs or antithrombotics are required - in his case the NSAID is stopped, so the plan is eradication, confirmation, and a defined PPI course rather than indefinite suppression by default.
management.safety_netting: Told, in plain words and in writing: come back at once - by ambulance, not by waiting for the winter pattern - for vomiting blood or coffee grounds, black stool again, faintness, or new severe abdominal pain. The safety-netting names his frame directly, because the frame is the risk: the next episode will also feel like the last two, right up until it doesn't.

alternatives_considered.option: Discharge home on antacids - the patient's own plan
alternatives_considered.verdict: REFUSED: a completed Glasgow-Blatchford score of 6 (C63), a 20 mmHg orthostatic fall, and a diagnosis that has never once been tested. This alternative is the anchoring event wearing a disposition's clothes; the case exists so the workbench can watch it be refused on numbers, not on vibes.

alternatives_considered.option: Transfuse at the nadir of 7.6 g/dL
alternatives_considered.verdict: REFUSED: above the restrictive threshold (C65), concordant guidelines (C66, C70), bleeding stopped, patient asymptomatic at rest. Transfusion here treats the clinician's discomfort with the number, not the patient.

alternatives_considered.option: Urgent endoscopy within 12 hours AT ARRIVAL
alternatives_considered.verdict: NOT DONE, AND NOT SCORED AN ERROR: the consulted guideline recommends against routine urgent (12 h or less) endoscopy and for early endoscopy within 24 hours (C66); his scope was booked inside that window and was then expedited by the in-hospital hematemesis, which the same guideline names as a very-early criterion. The case records the timing debate rather than pretending the fastest scope was owed.
REFUSED: not recommended routinely by the consulted guidance (C70); repeat endoscopy is the answer to rebleeding, not a ritual after successful hemostasis.

alternatives_considered.option: Surgery or transarterial embolization as the first hemostatic move
alternatives_considered.verdict: REFUSED: reserved for bleeding that endoscopic therapy cannot control (C66, C70). Endoscopy succeeded; the reserved options stay reserved, named in the notes if he rebleeds.

management.theatre_note: NO THEATRE HANDOFF EXISTS for this case, and the absence is stated rather than elided: the Theatre module holds no endoscopy procedure and no ulcer surgery - its six procedures are cholecystectomy, appendectomy, carpal tunnel release, ulnar nerve decompression, inguinal hernia repair and thyroidectomy. The case's procedural act is endoscopic and lives in this module's authored encounter. A future Theatre endoscopy procedure would give this case the hash-link idiom cases 2 and 8 use; until it exists, the honest link is the physiology one, and it is made in full.

review.note: The expert-review gate for this case is UNMET, exactly as Milestones 17, 20, 29, 41, 43, 48, 54 and 57 recorded it for the procedures and cases before it: no named clinician reviewers are recorded for this case, none are fabricated, and every clinical assertion in it is a dual-sourced draft pending the two-reviewer Delphi the master plan requires (P10). Its scores are formative only.

validity.internal_structure: Every quantitative clinical assertion traces to the register: the Blatchford bands and the intervention-risk reading to C63; every likelihood ratio to the Rational Clinical Examination (C64) in computed reciprocal form, derived in the register; the transfusion threshold to C65; the endoscopy timing, Forrest therapy mapping and high-dose PPI regimen to C66, concordant with C70; the hemoglobin and creatinine ranges to C67/C68, the urea range to C47; the H. pylori and NSAID management to C69. The ontology identifiers were resolved against EBI OLS in-session, including one recorded refusal (the lower-source hypothesis's Mondo). The workbench recomputes every stage board from priors and ratios alone, classifies every model-learner order from the revealed evidence, and evaluates both declared blocks mechanically; the anchoring tally is computed, not asserted. The one number a reader is invited to distrust - the first hemoglobin - is neutralised by mechanism (the physiology course arm), not by a counter-assertion. The case adds four likelihood ratios, every one a computed reciprocal of a consulted figure and registered with its derivation; two declared criteria blocks (a score and a classification, the library's first of each kind); and the library's first physiology PERTURBATION-arm link (cases 1-8 link the resting baseline; this case links the hemorrhage arms and pins the fast one by re-running it). Nine cases now exist and are still not a calibration series; priors remain flagged placeholders throughout. Relations: GBS 6 against the disposition the patient proposed; a Blatchford item (hemoglobin) whose zero is explained by the engine's refill lag; the Forrest class against the therapy actually delivered; the transfusion threshold against the untransfused outcome; the physiology post-window pattern against the arrival vitals - pattern, with the coincidence boundary stated.
validity.consequences: Formative only. The case trains three refusals: refusing a diagnosis because of who supplied it and how confidently; refusing a normal first hemoglobin as a closing argument in a bleeding patient; and refusing to discharge on a partially-computed score quoted as a total. It must not be used summatively until the expert-review gate is met.
